jobs.title: Team Lead Backend Engineer (Core Applications)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
HockeyStack is building the agent infrastructure for enterprise revenue. We spent five years building the only data architecture that preserves causality across the full revenue stack — every interaction, every signal, in sequence. On top of that foundation, we built Nex-lm, a purpose-built AI engine that compiles natural language into deterministic agent workflows. The result is a platform that can extract the revenue blueprint from a company's data, encode it into repeatable automations, and execute it across sales, marketing, and customer success — consistently, at scale.

We are not building a dashboard tool with an AI feature. We are building the operating layer that replaces the human bottleneck in enterprise revenue organizations. This is a category being defined right now, and we intend to own it.

We have raised $50M+ from Bessemer Venture Partners, General Catalyst, Y Combinator, and others.

We operate fully in-person in San Francisco. We move fast and we hire people who want to win.

Since launching late 2023, we have grown to 8-figures in ARR, process over 60 TB of revenue data monthly, and we are working with some of the largest B2B companies in the world like Microsoft, Harvey, New Relic, Collibra, etc.

🚀 Your Mission

As the Backend Tech Lead on the Core Applications team, your mission is to architect and scale our core API infrastructure that powers mission-critical workflows for Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success teams. You’ll lead the engineering behind the services that serve 60+ TB of GTM data, delivering low-latency, high-availability APIs that expose deep buyer insights to our internal apps and customer-facing dashboards.

This is a defining opportunity for an engineer who wants to own massive data and API infrastructure, set a high bar for engineering excellence, and ship fast in a high-urgency environment.

🔧 What You’ll Do

  • Lead the design and development of APIs that expose GTM data to internal and external users.

  • Own end-to-end architecture for large-scale data access patterns, optimizing for performance, cost, and reliability.

  • Collaborate closely with AI, data, and frontend teams to ensure seamless integrations and clean API contracts.

  • Tackle complex problems like versioning, rate-limiting, auth, query complexity, and cache invalidation across a fast-evolving product surface.

  • Build internal tooling to improve engineering velocity and observability for our backend systems.

  • Drive engineering best practices, code quality, and testing in a fast-paced, high-output environment.

  • Mentor engineers and set the technical direction for the team.

🧬 What We’re Looking For

  • Ownership-first mindset — you take initiative, move fast, and figure things out

  • Thrive in early-stage, high-urgency environments where speed and impact matter

  • Fully committed to working in-person 5 days/week at our SF HQ

  • Curious, self-aware, and feedback-driven — you bring energy, not ego

  • See this role as a defining chapter — not a stepping stone or side quest

  • 5+ years of backend engineering experience, ideally with exposure to high-scale systems.

  • Deep experience with modern backend stacks – we use Node.js, ClickHouse and AWS

  • Strong understanding of API design principles, query optimization, and distributed systems.

  • You’ve worked with large-scale data systems (think TBs of data) and know how to manage performance, cost, and uptime at scale.

  • Startup mindset – you move fast, figure things out, and don’t wait to be told what to do.

  • Comfortable owning ambiguity – you define the problem, architect the solution, and ship the result.

✨ Why Join Now?

We’re at an inflection point. The product is proven, the market is massive, and the opportunity is wide open. You’ll be joining a company with real traction, rapid growth, and meaningful backing—where every person still shapes the outcome. This isn’t just a job. It’s a chance to build something category-defining with people who care deeply about doing it right.

As part of our San Francisco, California-based team, the salary range for this role is $200,000– $240,000 USD base pay annually, depending on experience and qualifications.

HockeyStack is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status. We celebrate diversity and are committed to fostering an inclusive environment for all employees.

🚀 Your Mission

HockeyStack is scaling rapidly, and we’re looking for an exceptional Executive Assistant to the CEO to act as a strategic partner and leverage multiplier for our founder and executive team.

This is not a traditional administrative role. You will anticipate needs, streamline operations, and ensure the CEO’s time and energy are focused on the highest-impact priorities. You’ll help turn strategic objectives into actionable plans, manage complex workflows, and keep the CEO and leadership team fully aligned.

You’ll operate at the center of the company, collaborating with investors, executives, customers, and partners. You should be highly organized, proactive, tech-savvy, and comfortable operating in a fast-moving, high-growth environment.

This is a high-trust, high-visibility role with direct exposure to company strategy and executive decision-making. Your impact will be felt across the entire company as you help the CEO execute with precision and scale.

🔧 What You’ll Do

  • Executive Support & Leverage

    • Act as a true partner to the CEO — managing priorities, context-switching, and execution follow-through.

    • Anticipate needs before they arise and proactively solve problems rather than just reacting to requests.

    • Ensure the CEO is prepared for all meetings with clear agendas, context, and materials.

    • Track action items and decisions to ensure nothing falls through the cracks.

  • Calendar, Scheduling & Time Management

    • Own the CEO’s calendar end-to-end — optimizing for focus, leverage, and impact.

    • Schedule complex meetings across time zones with executives, investors, customers, and partners.

    • Ruthlessly prioritize requests and protect the CEO’s time.

    • Continuously refine scheduling systems and workflows using modern tools and software.

  • Communication & Coordination

    • Serve as a key point of contact between the CEO and internal/external stakeholders.

    • Draft, edit, and manage emails, agendas, meeting notes, and internal updates.

    • Coordinate closely with the executive team to ensure alignment and follow-through.

    • Help drive clarity across the org by reinforcing priorities and expectations.

  • Operational Execution & Special Projects

    • Support company-wide initiatives and strategic projects directly with the CEO.

    • Help coordinate leadership meetings, offsites, board meetings, and investor interactions.

    • Assist with preparation of board decks, investor updates, and key presentations.

    • Leverage modern software tools (Notion, Google Sheets, Superhuman, etc.) to streamline workflows, track projects, and optimize operations.

    • Identify operational gaps and help build repeatable systems and processes.

  • Travel & Logistics

    • Manage all CEO travel logistics (domestic and international).

    • Ensure seamless planning for meetings, events, conferences, and offsites.

    • Handle expense tracking and administrative workflows with precision.

🧬 What We’re Looking For

  • 3–6+ years of experience as an Executive Assistant supporting a CEO or senior executive in a fast-paced, high-growth environment (startup experience strongly preferred).

  • Understands how a software company works at a high level — knows the business, priorities, and workflows without needing hand-holding.

  • Proactive and anticipatory — can foresee needs before they arise and act without waiting for instructions.

  • Exceptionally organized with world-class attention to detail.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

  • High emotional intelligence — able to handle sensitive information with discretion and judgment.

  • Tech-savvy and adaptable — comfortable using tools like Notion, Superhuman, Google Sheets, and other modern software to streamline work and keep the CEO and team organized.

  • Comfortable operating with ambiguity and in a fast-paced environment.

  • Ability to move fast, manage competing priorities, and stay calm under pressure.

  • In-person availability at our San Francisco HQ.

✨ Why Join Now?

We’re at an inflection point. The product is proven, the market is massive, and the opportunity is wide open. You’ll be joining a company with real traction, rapid growth, and meaningful backing—where every person still shapes the outcome. This isn’t just a job. It’s a chance to build something category-defining with people who care deeply about doing it right.

We’re building a high-performing, in-person culture at our San Francisco HQ, where the team collaborates shoulder-to-shoulder five days a week. The on target earnings range for this role is $80,000 to $120,000 USD, adjusted for location, experience, and qualifications.

HockeyStack is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status. We celebrate diversity and are committed to fostering an inclusive environment for all employees.

🚀 The Role

The CRO is running a transition. HockeyStack is moving from a GTM intelligence company to the agent company for enterprise GTM. That means a new sales motion, a new positioning, a new buyer, a new demo, and a new category narrative — all being built and proven simultaneously, while the existing business continues to grow.

The Chief of Staff is the force multiplier that makes this possible without the organization falling apart.

You will sit at the center of Sales, Marketing, RevOps, and CS. You will own the operating cadence of the GTM organization. You will translate the CRO’s priorities into structured execution. You will be the person who makes sure the most important things actually get done.

This is a high-trust, high-visibility role. You will have direct access to the CRO, the CEO, and the board-level narrative. You will see everything. You will be expected to operate with the judgment of a senior leader from day one.

🔧 What You’ll Do

GTM Operating Cadence

Pipeline reviews, forecast calls, QBRs, weekly revenue meetings, hot account reviews, launch coordination. Right now these happen inconsistently. You design the cadence, run it, and hold the organization to it. When the CRO walks into a room, everything is already in motion.

State of the Business

The CRO needs to know at any point — not weekly, not at QBR — exactly where the business stands. Pipeline coverage by segment. Conversion rates by stage. Agent motion metrics versus attribution motion metrics. Ramp progress. Deal velocity. Churn signals. You own the unified metrics framework. You own the narrative. You are the person who sees a number moving wrong and raises it before it becomes a crisis.

OKR Execution

Quarterly goals at HockeyStack are not aspirations. They are commitments with owners, milestones, and accountability structures. You run the OKR cycle end-to-end — translating CRO priorities into workstreams, tracking execution, and surfacing what is off track before it is too late to fix.

Cross-Functional Alignment

The agents motion touches every team. Product is building the cockpit and the blueprint discovery layer. Marketing is repositioning the company. Sales is running founder-led conversations to prove the motion before scaling it. RevOps is rebuilding the data model. Finance needs the story for the fundraise. All of these teams need to move in the same direction at the same time. That coordination does not happen by accident. You own it.

Strategic Projects

New segment design. Pricing architecture. Competitive positioning analysis. Partner strategy. Launch playbooks. The CRO initiates projects that do not fit neatly into any existing team’s remit. You lead them end-to-end — from framing the problem through execution — and you deliver outputs that are ready for high-stakes decisions.

🧬 What We’re Looking For

You have 3 to 6 years of Chief of Staff experience inside a high-growth B2B SaaS company. You know what a GTM organization looks like when it is working and when it is not. You have built operating cadences, run OKR cycles, and managed cross-functional initiatives that required you to influence without authority.

Beyond the resume, a few things will determine whether this is the right role:

  • You think in systems. You do not just solve the problem in front of you — you build the infrastructure that prevents the next ten problems.

  • You move fast and you are comfortable with ambiguity. The agents motion is being built in real time. The playbook does not fully exist yet.

  • You have strong opinions and you will share them. The CRO does not want a coordinator. He wants a thought partner who pushes back when something is wrong.

  • You are deeply organized without being bureaucratic. Process exists to create speed, not slow things down.

  • You can hold a strategic conversation with a CRO and a tactical conversation with an AE in the same afternoon. The range is required.

  • You want to build something genuinely important. Not a feature. Not a vertical SaaS tool. The category-defining infrastructure for the next generation of enterprise software.

We’re at an inflection point. The product is proven, the market is massive, and the opportunity is wide open. You’ll be joining a company with real traction, rapid growth, and meaningful backing—where every person still shapes the outcome. This isn’t just a job. It’s a chance to build something category-defining with people who care deeply about doing it right.

As part of our San Francisco, California-based team, the on target earnings range for this role is $120,000– $160,000 USD annually, depending on experience and qualifications.

🎯 Your Mission

As HockeyStack's first dedicated HR Manager, your mission is to professionalize our people operations while protecting the DNA that got us here. You'll operationalize the HR infrastructure that enables us to scale with speed, precision, and care, transforming ad hoc processes into systematic excellence without losing our founder-led intensity.

You'll be the architect of our people systems, the coach to our managers, and the guardian of our culture. This role sits at the intersection of builder and operator: you'll design frameworks from scratch, train managers on leadership development, handle sensitive employee situations with grace, and ensure compliance as we grow.

You're not here to slow things down. You'll work hand-in-hand with our Head of Finance to transition HR ownership, establish accountability structures, and create the infrastructure that lets HockeyStack remain a world-class place to work at scale.

🔥 What You'll Do

  • Build HR Infrastructure From the Ground Up

    • Design, implement, and improve core HR policies, employee handbook, and compliance frameworks that scale with our growth.

    • Establish performance management systems that drive accountability, development, and alignment across all teams.

    • Create onboarding and offboarding processes that reflect HockeyStack's standards for speed, clarity, and candidate experience.

    • Build employee relations frameworks for conflict resolution, workplace investigations, and sensitive issue management.

    • Partner with Finance to ensure seamless payroll, benefits administration, and compliance filing processes.

  • Develop and Coach Managers Across the Organization

    • Design and deliver manager training programs covering employee management fundamentals, performance conversations, feedback delivery, and termination protocols.

    • Provide 1:1 coaching to hiring managers navigating difficult conversations, performance issues, and team dynamics.

    • Build frameworks and toolkits that empower managers to lead with confidence, clarity, and consistency.

    • Establish regular manager calibration sessions to ensure fairness and alignment in performance evaluations and compensation decisions.

  • Own Employee Relations and Workplace Culture

    • Serve as a trusted advisor for employees navigating workplace concerns, interpersonal conflicts, and career development.

    • Conduct workplace investigations with impartiality, thoroughness, and confidentiality.

    • Partner with leadership to evolve HockeyStack's culture as we scale, balancing our founder-speed DNA with the structure needed for sustainable growth.

    • Identify early warning signs of cultural drift, manager burnout, or team dysfunction and intervene proactively.

  • Drive Compliance, Risk Management, and Process Discipline

    • Ensure HockeyStack remains compliant with federal, state, and local employment laws across all jurisdictions where we operate.

    • Manage employee documentation, I-9 verification, and audit-ready recordkeeping.

    • Partner with legal counsel on employment contracts, termination protocols, and risk mitigation strategies.

    • Build reporting dashboards for headcount, attrition, performance trends, and key people metrics.

🚀 What We're Looking For

  • A Builder Who Thrives in Zero-to-One Environments

    • 5-7+ years of HR experience in high-growth startups, with at least 2 years building HR infrastructure from scratch or in early-stage environments.

    • Proven ability to design and implement people systems that balance operational rigor with startup agility.

    • Deep expertise in employment law, compliance, performance management, and employee relations.

  • An Operator Who Moves Fast Without Breaking Things

    • You move with urgency but never sacrifice precision, especially when it comes to compliance, terminations, or sensitive employee matters.

    • Exceptional judgment in high-stakes situations: you know when to escalate, when to coach, and when to intervene directly.

    • Strong project management skills with a track record of delivering complex, cross-functional people initiatives on tight timelines.

  • A Coach Who Develops First-Time Managers Into Leaders

    • Experience designing and delivering manager training programs that create lasting behavior change.

    • Natural coaching instincts: you can diagnose management gaps, deliver actionable feedback, and build confidence in leaders who are learning on the job.

    • Comfortable providing direct, candid guidance to founders, executives, and managers at all levels.

  • A Culture Steward Who Protects What Makes Us Special

    • You understand the difference between "adding process" and "slowing things down"; you build systems that enable speed, not bureaucracy.

    • Deep empathy for the employee experience combined with the backbone to make tough, principled decisions.

    • Passionate about maintaining high performance standards while fostering inclusivity, psychological safety, and belonging.

  • A Strategic Partner With Finance and Operations Fluency

    • Comfortable working alongside Finance on payroll, benefits, comp modeling, and headcount planning.

    • Data-driven mindset: you use metrics to diagnose problems, measure impact, and communicate ROI to leadership.

    • Strong written and verbal communication skills. You can craft policies, deliver presentations, and facilitate difficult conversations with equal skill.

You'll be joining a company with real traction, rapid growth, and meaningful backing—where every person still shapes the outcome. This isn't just a job. It's a chance to build something category-defining with people who care deeply about doing it right.

As our first HR Manager, you'll have outsized influence on the culture, systems, and leadership development that will define HockeyStack for years to come.
